sanskrit: tad bhavān ṛṣisaṃghasya hitārthaṃ sarvacoditaḥ yathādṛṣṭaṃ hṛṣīkeśe sarvam ākhyātum arhati
english: Therefore, urged by all, you should relate everything for the welfare of the assembly of sages, just as you witnessed it concerning Hṛṣīkeśa.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa munibhir nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ kathayām āsa devarṣiḥ pūrvavṛttāṃ kathāṃ śubhām
english: Thus addressed by the sages, the blessed seer Nārada, the divine sage, narrated an auspicious tale of what had happened of old.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato nārāyaṇasuhṛn nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ śaṃkarasyomayā sārdhaṃ saṃvādaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the blessed seer Nārada, friend of Nārāyaṇa, recounted the dialogue of Śaṃkara with Umā.

sanskrit: tapaś cacāra dharmātmā vṛṣabhāṅkaḥ sureśvaraḥ puṇye girau himavati siddhacāraṇasevite
english: The righteous lord of the gods, marked with the bull, practised austerities upon the holy mountain Himavat, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: nānauṣadhiyute ramye nānāpuṣpasamākule apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇe bhūtasaṃghaniṣevite
english: Upon that lovely mountain, rich with manifold healing herbs, thronged with flowers of every kind, crowded with troops of Apsarases, and attended by hosts of spirits.

sanskrit: tatra devo mudā yukto bhūtasaṃghaśatair vṛtaḥ nānārūpair virūpaiś ca divyair adbhutadarśanaiḥ
english: There the god, filled with delight, was surrounded by hundreds of bands of spirits, of various forms and misshapen, divine and wondrous to behold.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghragajaprakhyaiḥ sarvajātisamanvitaiḥ kroṣṭukadvīpivadanair ṛkṣarṣabhamukhais tathā
english: Some resembling lions, tigers, and elephants, drawn from every species, some with the faces of jackals and leopards, others with the heads of bears and bulls.

sanskrit: ulūkavadanair bhīmaiḥ śyenabhāsamukhais tathā nānāvarṇamṛgaprakhyaiḥ sarvajātisamanvayaiḥ kiṃnarair devagandharvair yakṣabhūtagaṇais tathā
english: With terrible owl-faced ones, and others with the faces of hawks and vultures, resembling beasts of every hue and gathered from all kinds, together with Kiṃnaras, divine Gandharvas, and hosts of Yakṣas and spirits.

sanskrit: divyapuṣpasamākīrṇaṃ divyamālāvibhūṣitam divyacandanasaṃyuktaṃ divyadhūpena dhūpitam tat sado vṛṣabhāṅkasya divyavāditranāditam
english: That assembly-hall of the bull-bannered god was strewn with divine flowers, adorned with divine garlands, anointed with divine sandal, fumed with divine incense, and resounding with divine music.

sanskrit: mṛdaṅgapaṇavodghuṣṭaṃ śaṅkhabherīnināditam nṛtyadbhir bhūtasaṃghaiś ca barhiṇaiś ca samantataḥ
english: It rang with the beat of drums and tabors and the blare of conches and kettledrums, with troops of spirits and peacocks dancing on every side.

sanskrit: pranṛttāpsarasaṃ divyaṃ divyastrīgaṇasevitam dṛṣṭikāntam anirdeśyaṃ divyam adbhutadarśanam
english: There the Apsarases danced; the divine place was attended by throngs of celestial women, lovely to the eye, indescribable, divine, and wondrous to behold.

sanskrit: sa giris tapasā tasya bhūteśasya vyarocata
english: By the austerity of that lord of beings, the mountain shone resplendent.

sanskrit: svādhyāyaparamair viprair brahmaghoṣair vināditaḥ ṣaṭpadair upagītaiś ca mādhavāpratimo giriḥ
english: Resounding with the Vedic chants of brahmins devoted to recitation, and with the humming of bees, the mountain was matchless as the springtime.

sanskrit: taṃ mahotsavasaṃkāśaṃ bhīmarūpadharaṃ punaḥ dṛṣṭvā munigaṇasyāsīt parā prītir janārdana
english: Beholding that place, resembling a great festival yet bearing a terrible aspect, the host of sages was filled with supreme delight, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: munayaś ca mahābhāgāḥ siddhāś caivordhvaretasaḥ maruto vasavaḥ sādhyā viśvedevāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: The illustrious sages, and the Siddhas of unbroken chastity, the Maruts, the Vasus, the Sādhyas, and the eternal Viśvedevas;

sanskrit: yakṣā nāgāḥ piśācāś ca lokapālā hutāśanāḥ bhāvāś ca sarve nyagbhūtās tatraivāsan samāgatāḥ
english: The Yakṣas, Nāgas, and Piśācas, the guardians of the worlds, the fires, and all the elemental beings, humbled, were gathered there together.

sanskrit: ṛtavaḥ sarvapuṣpaiś ca vyakiranta mahādbhutaiḥ oṣadhyo jvalamānāś ca dyotayanti sma tad vanam
english: The seasons scattered all their flowers, marvellous beyond measure, and the herbs, blazing with light, illumined that forest.

sanskrit: vihagāś ca mudā yuktāḥ prānṛtyan vyanadaṃś ca ha giripṛṣṭheṣu ramyeṣu vyāharanto janapriyāḥ
english: And the birds, filled with joy, danced and sang, calling out upon the lovely mountain slopes, beloved of all.

sanskrit: tatra devo giritaṭe divyadhātuvibhūṣite paryaṅka iva vibhrājann upaviṣṭo mahāmanāḥ
english: There upon the mountain-slope, adorned with divine minerals, the high-souled god sat, shining as upon a couch.

sanskrit: vyāghracarmāmbaradharaḥ siṃhacarmottaracchadaḥ vyālayajñopavītī ca lohitāṅgadabhūṣaṇaḥ
english: Clad in a tiger's skin, with a lion's hide for an upper garment, wearing a serpent for his sacred thread, and adorned with red armlets.

sanskrit: hariśmaśrur jaṭī bhīmo bhayakartā suradviṣām abhayaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ bhaktānāṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ
english: Tawny-bearded, matted-haired, terrible, a striker of fear into the foes of the gods, yet the giver of safety to all beings and to his devotees—he, the bull-bannered one.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tam ṛṣayaḥ sarve śirobhir avanīṃ gatāḥ vimuktāḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ kṣāntā vigatakalmaṣāḥ
english: Beholding him, all the seers touched the earth with their heads, and were released from every sin, made patient and freed from impurity.

sanskrit: tasya bhūtapateḥ sthānaṃ bhīmarūpadharaṃ babhau apradhṛṣyataraṃ caiva mahoragasamākulam
english: The abode of that lord of beings shone, bearing a terrible aspect, utterly unassailable, and teeming with great serpents.

sanskrit: kṣaṇenaivābhavat sarvam adbhutaṃ madhusūdana tat sado vṛṣabhāṅkasya bhīmarūpadharaṃ babhau
english: In a single moment, O slayer of Madhu, all became wondrous; that assembly of the bull-bannered god shone, bearing its terrible form.

sanskrit: tam abhyayāc chailasutā bhūtastrīgaṇasaṃvṛtā haratulyāmbaradharā samānavratacāriṇī
english: To him approached the daughter of the mountain, surrounded by troops of spirit-women, clad in raiment like Hara's own, observing the selfsame vow.

sanskrit: bibhratī kalaśaṃ raukmaṃ sarvatīrthajalodbhavam girisravābhiḥ puṇyābhiḥ sarvato 'nugatā śubhā
english: Bearing a golden pitcher brimming with the waters of all sacred fords, the fair goddess came, followed on every side by the holy mountain-streams.

sanskrit: puṣpavṛṣṭyābhivarṣantī gandhair bahuvidhais tathā sevantī himavatpārśvaṃ harapārśvam upāgamat
english: Raining down showers of flowers and manifold fragrances, frequenting the slopes of Himavat, she drew near to Hara's side.

sanskrit: tataḥ smayantī pāṇibhyāṃ narmārthaṃ cārudarśanā haranetre śubhe devī sahasā sā samāvṛṇot
english: Then, smiling, the fair-faced goddess, in sport, suddenly covered Hara's beautiful eyes with her two hands.

sanskrit: saṃvṛtābhyāṃ tu netrābhyāṃ tamobhūtam acetanam nirhomaṃ nirvaṣaṭkāraṃ tat sadaḥ sahasābhavat
english: But with his eyes thus covered, that whole assembly was at once plunged into darkness, senseless, void of oblation and of the cry of vaṣaṭ.

sanskrit: janaś ca vimanāḥ sarvo bhayatrāsasamanvitaḥ nimīlite bhūtapatau naṣṭasūrya ivābhavat
english: And all the people grew disheartened, seized with terror and dread; with the lord of beings' eyes shut, the world became as though the sun had perished.

sanskrit: tato vitimiro lokaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata jvālā ca mahatī dīptā lalāṭāt tasya niḥsṛtā
english: Then in an instant the world grew free of darkness, for a great blazing flame issued forth from his forehead.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ cāsya saṃbhūtaṃ netram ādityasaṃnibham yugāntasadṛśaṃ dīptaṃ yenāsau mathito giriḥ
english: And there arose upon him a third eye, like unto the sun, blazing as at the end of an age, by which that mountain was scorched.

sanskrit: tato girisutā dṛṣṭvā dīptāgnisadṛśekṣaṇam haraṃ praṇamya śirasā dadarśāyatalocanā
english: Then the mountain's daughter, beholding Hara whose eye was like blazing fire, bowed to him with her head and gazed with her wide eyes.

sanskrit: dahyamāne vane tasmin saśālasaraladrume sacandanavane ramye divyauṣadhividīpite
english: As that forest burned, with its sāla and pine trees, its lovely groves of sandal, lit up with divine herbs;

sanskrit: mṛgayūthair drutair bhītair harapārśvam upāgataiḥ śaraṇaṃ cāpy avindadbhis tat sadaḥ saṃkulaṃ babhau
english: That assembly grew crowded with herds of deer, fleeing in terror, drawing close to Hara's side, finding no refuge anywhere.

sanskrit: tato nabhaḥspṛśajvālo vidyullolārcir ujjvalaḥ dvādaśādityasadṛśo yugāntāgnir ivāparaḥ
english: Then with flames touching the sky, brilliant with quivering lightning-rays, like the twelve suns, like a second fire of the age's end—

sanskrit: kṣaṇena tena dagdhaḥ sa himavān abhavan nagaḥ sadhātuśikharābhogo dīnadagdhavanauṣadhiḥ
english: By that fire in a moment Himavat the mountain was scorched, its peaks and mineral expanses laid bare, its forests and herbs piteously burned.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mathitaṃ śailaṃ śailarājasutā tataḥ bhagavantaṃ prapannā sā sāñjalipragrahā sthitā
english: Seeing the mountain thus ravaged, the daughter of the king of mountains took refuge in the lord, standing with joined hands.

sanskrit: umāṃ śarvas tadā dṛṣṭvā strībhāvāgatamārdavām pitur dainyam anicchantīṃ prītyāpaśyat tato girim
english: Then Śarva, beholding Umā softened by her womanly nature, unwilling to see her father's distress, looked with affection upon the mountain.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavat punaḥ sarvaḥ prakṛtisthaḥ sudarśanaḥ prahṛṣṭavihagaś caiva prapuṣpitavanadrumaḥ
english: Then all became restored to its natural state, fair to behold, with its birds rejoicing and the forest trees in full flower.

sanskrit: prakṛtisthaṃ giriṃ dṛṣṭvā prītā devī maheśvaram uvāca sarvabhūtānāṃ patiṃ patim aninditā
english: Seeing the mountain restored, the blameless goddess, well pleased, addressed Maheśvara, the lord of all beings, her own lord.

sanskrit: bhagavan sarvabhūteśa śūlapāṇe mahāvrata saṃśayo me mahāñ jātas taṃ me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: O blessed lord of all beings, trident-bearer, of mighty vows, a great doubt has arisen in me; deign to explain it to me.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ te lalāṭe vai tṛtīyaṃ netram utthitam kimarthaṃ ca girir dagdhaḥ sapakṣigaṇakānanaḥ
english: For what reason did a third eye arise upon your forehead? And for what reason was the mountain burned, with its flocks of birds and its forests?

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ ca punar deva prakṛtisthaḥ kṣaṇāt kṛtaḥ tathaiva drumasaṃchannaḥ kṛto 'yaṃ te maheśvara
english: And for what reason, O god, was it again in a moment restored to its natural state, and clothed once more with trees by you, O Maheśvara?

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca netre me saṃvṛte devi tvayā bālyād anindite naṣṭālokas tato lokaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata
english: Maheśvara said: When my eyes were covered by you in childish play, O blameless goddess, the world at once lost its light and was plunged in an instant into darkness.

sanskrit: naṣṭāditye tathā loke tamobhūte nagātmaje tṛtīyaṃ locanaṃ dīptaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ te rakṣatā prajāḥ
english: When thus the sun was lost and the world turned to darkness, O daughter of the mountain, a blazing third eye was created by me, guarding the creatures for your sake.

sanskrit: tasya cākṣṇo mahat tejo yenāyaṃ mathito giriḥ tvatpriyārthaṃ ca me devi prakṛtisthaḥ kṣaṇāt kṛtaḥ
english: Great was the splendour of that eye, by which this mountain was scorched; and to please you, O goddess, it was in a moment restored to its natural state.

sanskrit: umovāca bhagavan kena te vaktraṃ candravat priyadarśanam pūrvaṃ tathaiva śrīkāntam uttaraṃ paścimaṃ tathā
english: Umā said: O blessed one, by what cause is your eastern face like the moon, lovely to behold, and likewise the northern, the western so beautiful?

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ ca mukhaṃ raudraṃ kenordhvaṃ kapilā jaṭāḥ kena kaṇṭhaś ca te nīlo barhibarhanibhaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: And by what cause is the southern face terrible? Why upward stand your tawny matted locks? And by what cause was your throat made blue like a peacock's plume?

sanskrit: haste caitat pinākaṃ te satataṃ kena tiṣṭhati jaṭilo brahmacārī ca kimartham asi nityadā
english: And by what cause does this Pināka ever rest in your hand? And why are you forever matted-haired and a celibate?

sanskrit: etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ sarvaṃ vada bhūtapate 'nagha sadharmacāriṇī cāhaṃ bhaktā ceti vṛṣadhvaja
english: Resolve for me all this doubt, O sinless lord of beings; for I am your companion in dharma and your devotee, O bull-bannered one.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa bhagavāñ śailaputryā pinākadhṛk tasyā vṛttyā ca buddhyā ca prītimān abhavat prabhuḥ
english: Thus addressed by the mountain's daughter, the blessed wielder of Pināka, the lord, was pleased by her conduct and her wisdom.

sanskrit: tatas tām abravīd devaḥ subhage śrūyatām iti hetubhir yair mamaitāni rūpāṇi rucirānane
english: Then the god said to her: "O fair one, listen: by what reasons these forms of mine arose, O lovely-faced one."

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca tilottamā nāma purā brahmaṇā yoṣid uttamā tilaṃ tilaṃ samuddhṛtya ratnānāṃ nirmitā śubhā
english: Maheśvara said: Of old, an excellent woman named Tilottamā, fair of form, was fashioned by Brahmā, who took up sesame-grain by sesame-grain from among precious things.

sanskrit: sābhyagacchata māṃ devi rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi pradakṣiṇaṃ lobhayantī māṃ śubhe rucirānanā
english: She approached me, O goddess, peerless in beauty upon the earth, circling me reverently, alluring me, O fair and lovely-faced one.

sanskrit: yato yataḥ sā sudatī mām upādhāvad antike tatas tato mukhaṃ cāru mama devi vinirgatam
english: From whichever side that fair-toothed one drew near to me, from that side, O goddess, a lovely face came forth upon me.

sanskrit: tāṃ didṛkṣur ahaṃ yogāc caturmūrtitvam āgataḥ caturmukhaś ca saṃvṛtto darśayan yogam ātmanaḥ
english: Wishing to behold her, by my yoga I attained a fourfold form and became four-faced, displaying the power of my yoga.

sanskrit: pūrveṇa vadanenāham indratvam anuśāsmi ha uttareṇa tvayā sārdhaṃ ramāmy aham anindite
english: With my eastern face I rule over Indra's domain; with the northern I take my delight together with you, O blameless one.

sanskrit: paścimaṃ me mukhaṃ saumyaṃ sarvaprāṇisukhāvaham dakṣiṇaṃ bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ raudraṃ saṃharati prajāḥ
english: My western face is benign, bringing happiness to all living beings; the southern, terrible to look upon and fierce, destroys the creatures.

sanskrit: jaṭilo brahmacārī ca lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā devakāryārthasiddhyarthaṃ pinākaṃ me kare sthitam
english: Matted-haired and celibate am I, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds; and for the accomplishment of the gods' purposes the Pināka rests in my hand.

sanskrit: indreṇa ca purā vajraṃ kṣiptaṃ śrīkāṅkṣiṇā mama dagdhvā kaṇṭhaṃ tu tad yātaṃ tena śrīkaṇṭhatā mama
english: Of old, Indra, coveting glory, hurled his thunderbolt at me; it scorched my throat and passed away, and thence came my name Śrīkaṇṭha.

sanskrit: umovāca vāhaneṣu prabhūteṣu śrīmatsv anyeṣu satsu te kathaṃ govṛṣabho deva vāhanatvam upāgataḥ
english: Umā said: When there are many other splendid mounts to be had, O god, how did the bull come to be your vehicle?

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca surabhīṃ sasṛje brahmāmṛtadhenuṃ payomucam sā sṛṣṭā bahudhā jātā kṣaramāṇā payo 'mṛtam
english: Maheśvara said: Brahmā created Surabhī, the cow of nectar, the giver of milk; once created, she multiplied manifold, streaming forth milk like nectar.

sanskrit: tasyā vatsamukhotsṛṣṭaḥ pheno madgātram āgataḥ tato dagdhā mayā gāvo nānāvarṇatvam āgatāḥ
english: The foam dropped from the mouth of her calf fell upon my body; then in anger I scorched the cows, and they took on their many colours.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ lokaguruṇā śamaṃ nīto 'rthavedinā vṛṣaṃ cemaṃ dhvajārthaṃ me dadau vāhanam eva ca
english: Then I was brought to peace by the world's teacher, who knew what was fitting; and he gave me this bull for my banner and for my mount.

sanskrit: umovāca nivāsā bahurūpās te viśvarūpaguṇānvitāḥ tāṃś ca saṃtyajya bhagavañ śmaśāne ramase katham
english: Umā said: Your dwellings are of many forms, endowed with every kind of quality; forsaking these, O blessed one, how is it that you delight in the cremation-ground?

sanskrit: keśāsthikalile bhīme kapālaghaṭasaṃkule gṛdhragomāyukalile citāgniśatasaṃkule
english: Terrible, strewn with hair and bones, crowded with skulls like potsherds, teeming with vultures and jackals, thronged with the fires of a hundred pyres;

sanskrit: aśucau māṃsakalile vasāśoṇitakardame vinikīrṇāmiṣacaye śivānādavinādite
english: Unclean, strewn with flesh, miry with marrow and blood, littered with heaps of carrion, resounding with the howls of jackals.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca medhyānveṣī mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ vicarāmi niśāsv aham na ca medhyataraṃ kiṃ cic chmaśānād iha vidyate
english: Maheśvara said: Seeking the pure, I roam the whole earth by night, and nothing more pure than the cremation-ground is to be found here.

sanskrit: tena me sarvavāsānāṃ śmaśāne ramate manaḥ nyagrodhaśākhāsaṃchanne nirbhuktasragvibhūṣite
english: Therefore, of all dwellings, my mind delights in the cremation-ground, shaded by the branches of the banyan, adorned with cast-off garlands.

sanskrit: tatra caiva ramante me bhūtasaṃghāḥ śubhānane na ca bhūtagaṇair devi vināhaṃ vastum utsahe
english: And there too my hosts of spirits take their delight, O fair-faced one; nor can I, O goddess, bear to dwell apart from my spirit-troops.

sanskrit: eṣa vāso hi me medhyaḥ svargīyaś ca mato hi me puṇyaḥ paramakaś caiva medhyakāmair upāsyate
english: This dwelling I hold to be pure and heavenly; holy and supreme, it is frequented by those who seek purity.

sanskrit: umovāca bhagavan sarvabhūteśa sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ vara pinākapāṇe varada saṃśayo me mahān ayam
english: Umā said: O blessed lord of all beings, foremost of all upholders of dharma, Pināka-handed giver of boons, this great doubt is mine.

sanskrit: ayaṃ munigaṇaḥ sarvas tapas tapa iti prabho taponveṣakaro loke bhramate vividhākṛtiḥ
english: This whole host of sages, O lord, crying "Austerity! Austerity!", wanders through the world seeking austerity in manifold forms.

sanskrit: asya caivarṣisaṃghasya mama ca priyakāmyayā etaṃ mameha saṃdehaṃ vaktum arhasy ariṃdama
english: For the sake of this assembly of seers, and to please me, O subduer of foes, deign to resolve this doubt of mine here.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ kiṃlakṣaṇaḥ proktaḥ kathaṃ vācarituṃ naraiḥ śakyo dharmam avindadbhir dharmajña vada me prabho
english: By what marks is dharma declared? And how can it be practised by men who have not found dharma? O knower of dharma, tell me, O lord.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tato munigaṇaḥ sarvas tāṃ devīṃ pratyapūjayat vāgbhir ṛgbhūṣitārthābhiḥ stavaiś cārthavidāṃ vara
english: Nārada said: Then the whole host of sages honoured the goddess in return with words adorned by the meaning of Ṛc-verses and with hymns, O best of those who know the truth.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca ahiṃsā satyavacanaṃ sarvabhūtānukampanam śamo dānaṃ yathāśakti gārhasthyo dharma uttamaḥ
english: Maheśvara said: Non-injury, truthful speech, compassion for all beings, self-control, and giving according to one's power—this is the highest dharma of the householder.

sanskrit: paradāreṣv asaṃkalpo nyāsastrīparirakṣaṇam adattādānaviramo madhumāṃsasya varjanam
english: No thought toward another's wife, protection of women left in trust, abstaining from taking what is not given, and shunning honey-wine and meat;

sanskrit: eṣa pañcavidho dharmo bahuśākhaḥ sukhodayaḥ dehibhir dharmaparamaiḥ kartavyo dharmasaṃcayaḥ
english: This fivefold dharma, of many branches, yielding happiness, is the store of merit to be heaped up by embodied beings devoted to dharma.
